intro: Range rules form a conjunction: a record is retained only if every configured field is valid and within bounds. Checking only one field would allow partially invalid rows through.
task: Retain numeric records satisfying every configured field range.
requirements: ranges maps field names to [low, high] finite numeric inclusive bounds with low <= high. Each record must contain numeric values for every configured field. Return copied records satisfying all ranges; empty ranges keeps all rows.

Sequence inputs are Python lists or tuples of at most 1000 items. Text inputs contain valid Unicode scalar characters and at most 10000 characters. Identifier and dictionary keys are nonempty strings of at most 100 characters. Numeric values are finite Python ints or floats with magnitude at most 1e9; bool is not numeric. Plain record data may contain strings, numbers, booleans, None, lists, tuples, and dictionaries; nesting is limited to six levels and dictionaries to 1000 keys.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: Validate bounds once, then require every configured field to pass.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: Endpoints are included; use <= on both sides of the comparison.

explanation: Range rules form a conjunction: a record is retained only if every configured field is valid and within bounds. Checking only one field would allow partially invalid rows through.
Validation is independent of filtering. A missing or nonnumeric field is a malformed input, even if another condition would already exclude that row.
